question.text: Member audit or inspection requirements for commodity derivative transactions include:

answer.text: Verification of compliance with exchange rules, correct margin collection, proper accounting, and maintenance of records
No special audit or inspection requirements
Only checking if CTT was paid

explanation.text: The Logic: Audits or inspections of members in commodity derivatives focus on verifying compliance with exchange rules, correct collection of margins from clients, proper accounting treatment of transactions, and maintenance of prescribed books and records. The Trap: Member audit scope is not limited to CTT payment or to year-end balances. Hedge-accounting documentation is a separate condition for applying hedge accounting and is not, by itself, listed as a transaction audit requirement at the member level. Note: Keeping reconcilable exchange statements, client margin records and settlement confirmations is the practical way to evidence the items examined in member audits or inspections.
